R-01: Halcyon Biologics Site 9 presented itself as a Level 4 government lab under a Department of Health Security contract, building pandemic cures.
R-02: On April 1 Ashby of Anvil Holdings signed in to see Director Marsh and never signed out; a DHS audit that day was postponed by Marsh.
R-03: A guard note says the vault cannot open from inside without the override, the dead bang on it nonstop, and a keycard is in the desk drawer.
R-04: The canteen menu for April 6 shows supply trucks stopped arriving that week and the kitchen fell back on reserve stock.
R-05: Tomas Ruiz from Security threw Dr. Hannah Cole a chocolate birthday cake on March 28, and Gus was known for stealing the corner pieces.
R-06: A worker named Danny wrote his mom in Macon that something was wrong, the Director hadn't left her office in days; the letter was never sent.
R-07: Lab tech R. Albrecht wrote a resignation to Dr. Marsh after seeing a dispersal curve on the Containment board, but never handed it in.
R-08: A drawing from Dr. Reyes's daughter Lucy sits on his desk, with a sticky note hinting his password is her name plus the year she was born.
R-09: Only 4 percent of Site 9's money came from the government; the other 96 percent came from Anvil Holdings, whose seal is an anvil in a ring of stars.
R-10: Dr. Reyes admits G-Strain was never a cure: he built it to spread fast, kill nearly all and keep hosts walking; the client refused a kill switch.
R-11: A photo on Marsh's desk shows her sailing a boat named Southern Grace on Lake Lanier, the only place nobody could reach her.
R-12: A note from Claudia, Marsh's assistant, says IT reset Marsh's login and she set it back to the name of Marsh's boat, no spaces, all caps.
R-13: G-Strain was sold by Anvil as TALLOW, a weapon that wipes out a population but leaves buildings, power and roads intact, with three buyers waiting.
R-14: Marsh objected to a field test, but Ashby said the board insisted: the demonstration would be Cedar Ridge, a town of 4,100 with one water main.
R-15: Reyes and Cole wrote that the virus still carries a lock for an off-switch, and Program Lazarus meant to build the key on the Deep Lab bench.
R-16: Cole's diary says the cure must come from first-generation tissue from a Containment subject, and she was scratched and locked herself in cell 3.
R-17: Cole's last recording from cell 3, feverish and scared, tells whoever finds it where the Lazarus notes are and says she's sorry about the door.
R-18: Reyes recorded that the Cedar Ridge quarantine held four days, then the strain changed in the water, the dead got up, and it got away.
R-19: Dr. Okafor hid the last antivirals in the morgue's locked cold drawer, coded to the founding year on the plaque in Dr. Patel's office.
R-20: The morgue terminal shows drawer 7 was opened from the inside on April 29, and drawer 8 is a keypad-locked cold drawer kept at 4 degrees.
R-21: Kane re-coded the armoury weapons locker to his wedding anniversary, shown on the wedding photo pinned beside his duty report.
R-22: Security chief Kane drove water authority men to the Cedar Ridge pumping station on April 2 and watched them open a valve with a Halcyon cold case.
R-23: The camera log shows Claudia Price's badge opened the vault on August 9, and the panic room off the rec room has been cycling ever since.
R-24: Gus Delaney's note on the control console says the control room login is still Kane's, which he never changed in eleven years.
R-25: Ashby told Marsh the buyers loved the demonstration, refused to extract the staff, and ordered Site 9 sealed at midnight on May 2.
R-26: A recorded call has Ashby calmly telling Marsh that Site 9 had served its purpose, nobody was coming, and thanking her for her work.
R-27: Kane recorded that the site was sealed from outside on May 3; he was bitten and took keycard 3 with him, so you have to take it off his body.
R-28: The armoury inventory from May 2 lists only 3 pistols, 1 rifle and a shotgun with one box of shells left, and ammunition was already low.
R-29: Work order 0402-W had Gus Delaney put a sealed Halcyon cold case into the Cedar Ridge water main on April 2, on the Director's orders.
R-30: The emergency generator can power only three sectors at once, and powering Containment opens the cell doors for good.
R-31: Gus Delaney hid a food stash in a padlocked toolbox behind the boiler before heading for the far tunnels, and said to eat the peaches first.
R-32: The Maintenance crew safe room has a ration locker stocked to feed six people for ten days.
R-33: Subject 14 was Marcus Webb, a 34-year-old homeless man paid $400 a week as a volunteer, picked because he had no next of kin.
R-34: Marcus Webb's notebook tracks him going from steak dinners to shots, fever, peeling skin and endless hunger as he turned.
R-35: The Cedar Ridge plan expected 98 percent dead, burnout by day 9 behind an Anvil quarantine line, a chemical spill cover story, and no backup plan.
R-36: The cryo hall holds first-generation G-Strain samples and a portable cold case; cure tissue must be taken within a minute of death and kept cold.
R-37: Reyes explains making Lazarus: power the Deep Lab, two loud hours at the bench, three doses a batch, and test it on the analyser before trusting it.
R-38: Cole's first Lazarus trial made a subject lucid for hours before relapse, so every batch must be checked on the analyser and given before the turn.
R-39: Reyes, dying, said the cure works if given before the turn, but he took it too late, and he couldn't finish his message to Lucy.
R-40: Marsh confessed to the Anvil board that she released TALLOW at Cedar Ridge, it spread worldwide, 61 staff were sealed in, and the cure notes are here.
R-41: The staff directory lists Claudia Price as Marsh's executive assistant, with a photo of a dark-haired woman in a cardigan.
R-42: Marsh told Claudia to hide in the panic room off the rec room, which has its own air and six months of food, and to open it for no one.
